item.text: Victoria’s Royal Commission into Family Violence was asked to identify effective prevention, early intervention, victim support, perpetrator accountability and coordinated responses.
item.support: the Commission’s task was to identify the most effective ways to:

item.text: It examined the response across police, courts, support services, child protection and other government and community services.
item.support: develop and refine systemic responses to family violence

item.text: The Commission concluded that services were overwhelmed, responses were poorly coordinated, information sharing was inadequate and too little effort went into prevention and recovery.
item.support:
the Commission identified gaps and obstacles that are limiting the 
effective implementation of laws, policies, and programs:

item.text: Its 227 numbered recommendations seek stronger risk assessment and information sharing, better services and accountability, and sustained investment in prevention and response.
item.support:
The Victorian Government investigate options for increasing its capacity to invest in preventing 
and responding to family violence

item.quote:
Services are not currently equipped to meet this high level of demand, which 
undermines the safety of those experiencing family violence and their potential for recovery.

Victims are too often left to carry the 
burden of managing risk.
